Can a fly-brain model learn the German citizenship test?

New: the first learning result, replicated ↗

FLY-002 learned four directly stimulated neural patterns: 32/32 frozen trials, then 30/32 with new ensembles. The visual gate remains unresolved. The new lab note contains the film, calibration audit, controls, protocols and shareable story. The original visual failure remains documented below.

The question

A connectome-constrained model learning to recognize a finite question bank is a plausible engineering hypothesis. This project has not demonstrated it. A fly understanding German civic knowledge is a substantially stronger claim, with no supporting result in the studies reviewed here.

The useful research question is whether the measured fly wiring contributes to a model that can acquire the task, retain it, and pass a frozen evaluation. Neuron count alone does not answer that question. Neither does an attractive animation. The current implementation fails an elementary visual-learning check, so there is no defensible estimate of its time to a passing score.

There are three distinct targets. They require different evidence and should never share an undifferentiated “the fly learned German” label.

TargetWhat would countCurrent assessment
Visual associationLearn four visual categories and recognize new examples with feedback off.Biological motivation exists; this implementation scored 0/16.
Question-bank recognitionLearn public questions and answer content, then recognize them under fresh rendering and option order.A reasonable experiment. Feasibility and training duration remain unmeasured.
German comprehensionAnswer genuinely new questions and paraphrases using learned concepts.An open capability claim. Passing familiar catalogue items would not establish it.

The official test uses 33 four-option questions, including three state-specific items, with at least 17 correct within 60 minutes under supervision. The published catalogue is available for preparation; the official exam forms are not published. A software practice run can be compared with that threshold, but is not an official examination or certificate. [1]

Published findings

The new map is an anatomical resource

Google Research, HHMI Janelia and collaborators reported a male central nervous system reconstruction with more than 166,000 neurons and approximately 125 million synaptic connections. The map includes the brain and ventral nerve cord. The project catalogue identifies 11,691 cell types, allowing comparisons between shared, sex-specific and differently connected male and female circuits. These are structural findings; the publication does not report a citizenship-test learner. [2] [3]

The accompanying resource records a June 2026 v1.0 dataset release and September 2026 journal publication. This implementation uses MaleCNS v1.0. The 2024 FlyWire computational literature concerns a different connectome and must not be presented as validation of this male-CNS implementation. [4]

Simple models can make useful behavioral predictions

Shiu and colleagues built a brainwide leaky integrate-and-fire model from connectivity and predicted neurotransmitter identities. They tested predictions in feeding initiation and antennal grooming, including biological activation and silencing experiments. Across 164 tested predictions, 91% were consistent with their empirical results; the paper also reports 84% when a large optogenetic set is excluded. Those percentages concern the stated sensorimotor predictions, not arbitrary task learning or general intelligence. [5]

The authors’ software exposes neural activation, silencing, spike times and rates. Its existence demonstrates a usable experimental model, not an automatically trained organism. Our C++ kernel and sensory interface are a separate implementation with separate assumptions and require their own validation. [6]

Connectome-constrained visual networks can be trained

Lappalainen and colleagues modeled motion pathways covering 64 cell types. They optimized unknown cell and synapse parameters for visual motion estimation and compared predicted activity with measurements from 26 studies. This is meaningful evidence that anatomy can constrain a trainable computational model. It is not evidence for reading or citizenship knowledge. [7]

A crucial implementation detail is that the published pipeline includes a learned decoder. The official Flyvis tutorial trains network and decoder jointly; its displayed example has 734 free network parameters and 7,427 decoder parameters. These are the tutorial’s parameter counts, not neuron counts or a general statement about every Flyvis configuration. Copying that decoder into this project would change the “only the fly network makes the choice” experiment. A fixed measurement of designated neural outputs is a different readout design. [8]

Biological visual memory has specific circuitry

Vogt and colleagues identified visual projection pathways to a specialized mushroom-body region and visual responses in a subset of Kenyon cells. Perturbations affected visual memory of color or brightness. This gives a concrete reason to inspect the visual projection → visual Kenyon-cell route, rather than treating every mushroom-body neuron as an interchangeable input for text. These experiments establish sensory association in flies, not symbolic reasoning. [9]

Matching wiring does not uniquely determine activity

Beiran and Litwin-Kumar’s 2025 theoretical study found that recurrent networks with the same synaptic weights could still have different dynamics because of their biophysical parameters. Adding recordings from a subset of neurons could constrain those dynamics. For this project, biological fidelity therefore needs activity-level validation as well as anatomical fidelity. A successful engineered classifier and a faithful model of a fly are related research targets, but neither automatically establishes the other. [10]

Attempt 001 and its visual failure

The retained graph contains 166,700 neurons, 25,582,938 directed cell-to-cell edges and 124,177,617 synaptic contacts. An edge aggregates contacts between a pair of cells; the two counts describe different things. The display contains 630 sampled neuron skeletons, while the simulation uses the full retained graph. [11]

Question images are sampled at 3,335 inferred retinal positions. The neural dynamics run at a 0.1 ms integration step. Four fixed output populations · MBON11 through MBON14 · are assigned to A through D. The unique highest positive mean firing rate selects an answer; silence or a tie abstains. The input process has no OCR, language model, question-ID lookup, or access to the answer key. This makes the inference boundary explicit, but does not validate these particular sensory and output choices. [12]

Recorded stageResultInterpretation
Before learning0/8 visual trialsNo positive answer selection.
Feedback phase32 trials; zero weights changedThe specified learning rule did not update.
Held-out check0/16; gate requires 12Citizenship training was not started.
Untrained exam baseline0/33; 33 abstentionsA diagnostic baseline, not a trained attempt.

These records diagnose this implementation. They do not measure the limits of fly intelligence. The exam replay is kept as evidence of the input/output behavior of the frozen starting model. [13] [14]

Three actionable findings from the code and records

1. The update signal is zero. The proposed reward rule multiplies presynaptic and postsynaptic trial spike counts. The relevant memory and answer populations are silent in the recorded gate, so their product is zero and every candidate weight remains unchanged. Repeating the same silent conditions cannot turn this zero update into learning. This is an algebraic property of the implemented rule, not a conjecture about biological learning.

2. The input transform compresses contrast. The steady input drive is 30L / (0.02 + L), where L is normalized luminance. The rendered paper uses 238/255 and the main ink uses 18/255: a luminance ratio of 13.22. The corresponding drive values are 29.37 and 23.38, a ratio of 1.26. This is a diagnostic of our engineering transform; it is not a measured biological contrast-response curve. It does not by itself prove that all character information is lost.

3. More activity is not more discrimination. Multiplying all synaptic weights by two or four activates memory and answer populations, but both opposing probe patterns select A. At twofold gain, the leading output rates are 368.5 and 364 Hz. This reveals nonselective activity under those probes, not restored cognition. The gain probes were not substituted into the exam to produce a better-looking result. [15] [16]

A further uncertainty is neurotransmitter sign: 3,718 retained neurons have an unresolved or ambiguous sign in the current mapping and default to excitation. That policy should be examined through sensitivity analyses and cell-specific evidence. It cannot be validated merely because a simulation runs without errors. [11]

A training program that would answer the question

The next model revision should be a new, versioned experiment. The existing failed gate remains part of the record. Before any citizenship training, the revised model must demonstrate basic learning using a declared encoder, declared plastic synapses and a fixed output rule. The stages below are a proposed protocol, not completed results.

1. Establish a functioning sensory route

Measure responses to blank fields, contrast steps, moving bars and four spatial patches. Inspect retinal, lamina, visual projection, visual Kenyon-cell and output populations separately. Confirm that different stimuli create reproducibly different neural states and that activity reaches the proposed learning circuit. Compare response signs and time courses with published visual physiology where compatible data are available.

Revise the input response curve, cell dynamics or readout placement only using this development set. Keep input mapping independent of the answer labels. Record each change and its effect, including failures. The aim is a selective sensory representation with a usable learning signal; increasing global gain until everything fires is not an acceptance criterion.

2. Demonstrate elementary learning with controls

Train the four-category visual task with randomized position, size and luminance. Evaluate on fresh draws with feedback disabled. The current 12/16 threshold can remain a preliminary gate, but a credible result should replicate across at least five independently initialized or randomized runs and a larger preregistered test set. Five runs is a proposed development minimum, not a statistical guarantee.

Compare the trained model with unchanged weights, shuffled training labels, shuffled connectivity under a declared matching procedure, and a model with the claimed learning route silenced. These controls ask whether learning happened, whether target information leaked, and whether the fly wiring mattered. Diagnostic control models must be reported separately; their predictions must never become the fly’s answers.

3. Attempt catalogue learning as an explicit recognition task

Begin with a small, balanced subset of questions. If performance survives fresh rendering, expand the bank and measure a learning curve rather than selecting an attractive endpoint. Train on question-and-option content, not a numeric question ID. Keep the encoder fixed and label-independent; learned parameters must reside in the declared neural model.

Use fresh fonts, line breaks, layout variations and option permutations during evaluation. When option order changes, the model must select the correct answer content in its new position. Memorizing a fixed A/B/C/D label for each question would fail that test. Public catalogue study is legitimate for a recognition benchmark, but a test on familiar content must be described as such.

The current data pipeline includes only 239 eligible national text questions and seven eligible Berlin text questions. It excludes image items and items whose secondary answer key did not match. It therefore cannot yet support a full-catalogue claim. Complete and independently verify the question data before expanding the experiment to all relevant items. [17]

4. Treat comprehension as a separate investigation

Hold out entire question meanings, not merely different screenshots of the same item. Test paraphrases, reordered statements and new questions requiring the same concepts. Specify where German language knowledge enters training. If pretrained text embeddings or a language model are introduced, the system becomes a hybrid and must be reported that way; it no longer fulfills the strict fly-network-only objective.

No cited study supplies a validated recipe for this fourth stage. A sensible research program can attempt the narrower recognition target first while keeping the stronger language question open. The number of neurons does not provide a shortcut from visual learning to civic understanding.

How long would training take?

Time to pass is unknown. We can estimate the cost of a specified number of examples, but we do not yet know the examples required, whether the revised model will converge, or whether it can reach the target at all. The 60-minute test allowance is an inference constraint, not a training budget.

The recorded baseline processed 33 one-second neural trials in 57.102 seconds of wall time, or 1.73 seconds per example. The busiest recorded gain probe took 22.347 seconds for one simulated second. These are different activity regimes and workloads; they are useful scenario anchors, not a confidence interval or guaranteed lower and upper bounds. A future training implementation must be benchmarked directly. [14] [15]

Excludes development, dataset preparation, validation sweeps, retries and hardware changes. Multipliers are assumptions. No successful training run has measured them.

310-item scenarioExamplesQuiet forward costBusy forward cost
10 passes3,1001.49 hours19.24 hours
100 passes31,00014.90 hours192.43 hours
1,000 passes310,000149.00 hours1,924.33 hours

These scenarios assume one simulated second per example and sequential processing at the observed runtime. Longer temporal inputs multiply the cost. A differentiable optimizer, batching or a GPU changes both overhead and throughput; the present measurements do not justify a GPU price or speed claim. The first useful estimate of a real training schedule comes after a pilot measures learning progress and elapsed time on the intended hardware. [16]

Development time is a separate uncertainty. Sensory calibration, a stable learning rule, data verification and independent evaluation can dominate the computer’s runtime. A promised deadline such as “the fly will pass tomorrow” would currently be speculation. The concrete next milestone is a repeatable elementary learning result, followed by a measured small-bank pilot.

Evidence needed for a passing claim

One eye-catching score is insufficient. Freeze the model, encoder and readout before evaluation; hash the artifacts; predeclare the question sampling and stopping rule; and log every item, abstention, spike trace and elapsed time. Keep the grader separate. Report every preregistered evaluation, including failed seeds and failed exam forms.

For orientation, an idealized independent uniform guesser has a 0.0951% probability of reaching 17/33 in one attempt. Searching 1,000 independent attempts raises the chance of finding at least one apparent pass to about 61.4%. This is a mathematical example of selection bias, not an allegation about any particular viral demo. Real neural errors and question difficulties need not be independent. [16]

Assumed independent item accuracyProbability of ≥17/33
25%0.095%
50%50.0%
60%87.9%
70%99.2%

These values are binomial calculations, not measured model performance. They show why barely crossing the pass mark once is weaker evidence than robust item accuracy and repeatable performance. Report confidence intervals with the sampling unit stated; repeated screenshots of one question do not create independent question-level evidence.

A stronger scientific contribution would demonstrate both task performance and a causal role for the connectome. If a matched randomized network performs equally well, the result may still be an interesting engineered learner, but the special explanatory value of the fly wiring has not been established. If silencing the purported memory pathway leaves performance unchanged, the claimed mechanism needs revision.

The scientific journey on screen

The story begins with the original challenge: a fly trying to pass before a human. The next scene should make the experiment legible: show the exact stimulus, the recorded neural response, the feedback and any measured synaptic change. Then freeze the model, present the 33-question practice sitting, reveal its actual result and open the evidence.

The visual design can be cinematic while the data stay literal. The particle brain uses real sampled skeleton positions. Colored anatomy remains visible; recorded 20 ms bins brighten the cells that fired in the simulation. Continuous branches preserve the source skeleton topology during simplification. The 3D body’s articulated motion is illustrative. A head-aligned enlarged brain view is a display registration between different source specimens, not a claim of exact anatomical co-registration.

A result should answer a specific question: which route became active, which weights changed, what transferred to fresh examples, and what failed? The research notebook should distinguish the published connectome findings, our measured observations, and proposed experiments. A viral clip supplies a presentation reference; without inspectable code, training data and controlled evaluation it cannot verify where the task-solving computation occurred.

The justified headline today is a question: Can we train a fly-brain model to pass Germany’s citizenship test? A future positive result could support a precise statement about the tested recognition task and architecture. The broader comprehension claim would still require the separate evidence described above.
